summary: Switches between the sections of one page or object without leaving it: the Team, Reviews, Tools and You groups of Settings, the Usage, Tokens, Code and Changelog of a component. The selected tab is ink text over the signal underline; the others are muted text.
whenToUse: Two to seven sections or panels of one page or object, each with different content, where users switch back and forth: Settings (Team, Reviews, Tools, You), a component page (Usage, Tokens, Code, Changelog), the color families of the token editor.
The underline look, always. The contained variant is deprecated: it looked like a SegmentedControl, a third look for the same idea. A compact switch of a view or a filter is a SegmentedControl.
count to show how many items wait in a view, like open reviews.
Vertical orientation for settings pages with many sections next to their content.

tabId on a TabsPanel rendered outside its Tabs root, when the tabs are one island and the panels are not (a static page, panels holding islands of their own): show the picked one with showTabsPanel from @bridge-ds/react/dom.
whenNotToUse: Steps of a sequence the user must complete in order: use a stepper or a form with sections.
Navigation between pages with their own URL: use SidebarNav or links styled as tabs, not Tabs (which do not change the URL).
Switching a view or a filter of the same content (List, Grid or Board; the token type filter; Light or Dark; Side by side or Overlay; an expression picker): use SegmentedControl.
Changing a setting saved with a form: use RadioGroup.
A tab-like row built with your own CSS: never. A tab list is these Tabs, a view switch is a SegmentedControl, nothing in between.

dos.title: Short, parallel labels
dos.text: One or two nouns per tab, same grammatical form. The user scans them as a set.

dos.title: Counts sit in a count tag
dos.text: Pass count, never a number typed into the label: it renders as a small neutral tag after the label, centered on it, and looks the same on every tab, selected or not: only the label's ink follows the selection.

donts.title: Tabs that are really actions
donts.text: "Export" or "Delete" in a tab list hides an action behind a view switch. Use a Button.

accessibility: Base UI Tabs: role tablist, tab and tabpanel, aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby are wired for you.
One tab stop for the whole list. Arrow keys move between tabs (Up and Down when vertical), Home and End jump, focus wraps by default.
By default arrows move focus and Enter or Space selects; set activateOnFocus when panels are cheap to render.
Give the TabsList an aria-label (or labelledby) so the tablist has a name.
The selected tab has the signal underline plus ink text (the others are muted): never color alone, and never a box or an outline, which would read as focus.
The focus ring shows on keyboard focus only (:focus-visible), inside the tab a step off its edge; a click draws no ring.
Disabled tabs are announced as disabled and cannot be selected.

A TabsPanel outside its root is still a labelled tabpanel in the tab order: give it tabId (the Tab's id) and give that Tab aria-controls (the panel's id). Panels start shown, so a page without JavaScript reads them all.
contentGuidelines: No verbs, no punctuation, no more than two or three words.
Counts are numbers in the count prop, not in the label text.

anatomy.label: Label
anatomy.contained: Contained variant (deprecated: use underline Tabs for sections, SegmentedControl for a view or a filter)
anatomy.linked: Linked panel, outside the Tabs root (keeps the page's text size)
